subject: tu:game/sys/memcard
value:
A work order's mandated items MUST be screened against the CURRENT version of every record they rest on, at the moment the order is written - not against the version the dispatching integrator last read. Measured on run 38's memcard SOURCE lane: 3 of 3 mandated items had been executed or refuted by records ACCEPTED IN THE COMMIT IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING the one that staged the work claim, and the order still described them as open.

THE MECHANISM, which is what makes this different from ordinary staleness. The order cited run-31 records by their conclusions. Between run 31 and run 38 the corpus superseded all three: attempt.WS_writegauntletsave-...-v3 supersedes v2, attempt.WS_loadgauntletsave-...-v5 supersedes v4, attempt.MC_drawmemcardmessage-...-v1 supersedes attempt.HV_...-v2. The superseding records were accepted at 9e9d839bc ('Accept run-37 records (26; 6 work claims released)'), and the work claim was staged two commits later at 374141980. So the order was not written against an old graph - it was written against a CURRENT graph whose newest records were never re-read, because the order's author was working from the ITEM LIST rather than from the records. Version suffixes are the load-bearing detail: citing 'the WS record' is ambiguous across four versions and resolves, in practice, to whichever one the author remembers.

WHAT IT COST, itemised, because the failure is not free even when it is caught. Item 1 mandated 'the WS run-31 THREE-PIECE COMBINED APPLY, applied TOGETHER in one probe'; v3's attempted_axis records that it 'Executed the work order's THREE-PIECE COMBINED APPLY' and that the combined probe 'reproduced the record's own accounting exactly (+2, nothing closed)'. The lane was ordered to re-run a probe whose negative result was already accepted. Item 2 mandated 'the recorded addic-fusion trade'; v5's first line records that premise as 'REFUTED from the BASELINE residual itself, before any build was spent on a cure', because the baseline multiset contains no addic./cmplwi/cmpwi token at all. The lane was ordered to execute a premise the corpus had already measured false - the precise thing AGENTS.md discipline 5 forbids. Item 3's framing was the only sound one, and it was sound BECAUSE it quoted its record's newest version.

THE CHEAP FIX, one command per named function, and it is already in AGENTS.md's dispatch screens as 'One gdlmem context per function the order NAMES'. This law strengthens it to: the order must quote the record ID INCLUDING its version suffix for every premise it mandates, and any premise whose newest record carries outcome negative/capped, or a `refutes`/`supersedes` edge pointing at the cited version, is not dispatchable as open work. A brief that cannot name the version it is citing has not screened the record.

COROLLARY, and the reason a lane should not simply obey. Because the superseding records were accepted, their discipline-10b hypotheses were the ACTUAL mandatory step 1 for two of the three functions, and they are strictly better work than the order's items: v3's second-induction-variable hypothesis and v5's branch-site classification both come with a pre-registered cheapest refuting observation, and both resolved this run - one negative on a single probe, one buildless. Reading the newest record does not merely avoid waste, it substitutes a sharper task for a stale one.
